patch.value: Bridged history follow-ups: history diffs show unreconstructable before-values, and epoch-2 variant selection ignores distinguishing evidence

Raised by Codex review round 4 of the append-only bridge change (pm-gh1715) on 2026-11-21, deferred because none of the three loses data or serves a restore. (1) pm history --diff and computeHistoryDiff replay every entry without bridge or replay_inexact awareness. For a version inside a bridged or dissolved segment they report replay's before-value (the title before an out-of-band edit) as the historical before-value, although restore and get --at refuse that version with history_version_unreconstructable. Diff rows for such entries should report the before-value as unknown or carry an inexact flag. (2) resolveTailVariant picks the first index whose replay candidates contain the tail anchor. When an out-of-band edit added linked-test provenance and a later recorded change realigned replay, both epoch-2 variants can match on replay while only the field-frozen variant matches the on-disk item, so the appended record can take the expanded variant. Selection should compare the sets of matching indices and prefer distinguishing evidence. (3) verifyBridgeCloser accepts any candidate epoch and variant whose hash equals the closer's after_hash once the declared-epoch rule is satisfied. Where replay or the recorded tail proves the epoch or variant, the closer should be held to that surface, so an implicit stream cannot switch its bridge to epoch 1 or to the other epoch-2 variant. Duplicate check: searched history diff, bridge, replay_inexact, epoch-2 variant and closer surface; pm-gh1715 owns the bridge itself, and pm-rpucvb the double-fault salvage gap.

pm history --diff marks or blanks the before-value for every entry restore refuses as unreconstructable, proven by a spec over a bridged and a dissolved stream; resolveTailVariant prefers the variant set that distinguishes the tail over a duplicate replay match; verifyBridgeCloser holds the closer to the epoch and variant that replay or the recorded tail proves
Every history read that presents a historical state agrees with restore about which versions are exact
Diffs present replay's before-values for inexact versions, and variant selection can ignore distinguishing evidence

value.text: A fourth deferred case from Codex review round 6 of the same change, on 2026-11-21. Two clones repair the same out-of-band edit independently, giving equivalent bridges A and B. They merge in both directions (one result keeps A plus a neutral copy of B, the other B plus a neutral copy of A), each then records an ordinary update, and the two results are merged. The union retains repair order A then B on one side and B then A on the other, and the later updates keep the equivalent-bridge path from applying, so the merge driver refuses with "History union cannot preserve contradictory original branch event orders". It fails closed and loses nothing: the file stays unresolved for manual recovery. A fix normalizes a run of equivalent repairs (live or neutral) before ordering the later edits, keeping one live bridge and neutral copies for the other repairs' provenance.
